Query SingleStore as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__singlestore.R
oauth_db_singlestore.Rd

Query SingleStore or SingleStore Helios using each visitor's database privileges. The helper supplies their JWT access token to SingleStore's ODBC driver and returns a DBI connection for SQL or dbplyr queries.

Usage

oauth_db_singlestore(
  authorization,
  server,
  database = NULL,
  ...,
  ssl_ca,
  user = "*",
  driver = "SingleStore ODBC Unicode Driver",
  port = 3306L,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

server

One SingleStore SQL endpoint hostname or IPv4 address, without a protocol or port.

database

Optional default database. NULL uses the server default.

...

Result options timeout, timezone, timezone_out, bigint, encoding, name_encoding, interruptible, NO_CACHE, FORWARDONLY, and COMPAT_MODE. Authentication, routing, reconnect and TLS settings cannot be overridden.

ssl_ca

Path to a PEM file containing the trusted server CA chain. Required to enforce encrypted connections with the SingleStore driver.

user

SingleStore username, or a reactive function returning it. The default "*" lets SingleStore select the user from its trusted JWT mapping; this requires SingleStore 8.1.20 or later.

driver

Installed SingleStore ODBC driver name or library path. Use SingleStore Connector/ODBC 1.2.1 or later.

port

SQL endpoint port, default 3306.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A reactive function, usually named con. Call connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression, then pass the connection to DBI. Before sign-in, the function waits quietly.

Details

Install odbc and SingleStore's ODBC driver. Configure the database to trust your provider's JWT access tokens and map them to users created with authentication_jwt. Grant those users access to the app's data. The issuer, audience, scopes and username claim depend on that setup.

Create the helper inside server() and call con() before each query. Connections require TLS with certificate and hostname verification. Driver browser sign-in, keyring credentials and option files are disabled; shinyOAuth handles sign-in and token renewal.

A changed access token replaces the connection on the next con() call. Token renewal does not rerun completed reactive queries. Account or username changes, sign-out, lost permissions and session end close the connection. Failed queries are not replayed. Finish results and transactions before obtaining another connection after token renewal.

See also

vignette("singlestore", package = "shinyOAuthDB") for database setup, sign-in configuration and a complete Shiny app.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_singlestore(
  auth$connection,
  server = "workspace.example.singlestore.com",
  database = "reporting",
  ssl_ca = "path/to/ca.pem"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT CURRENT_USER() AS database_user")
})
} # }
